title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Work IQ REST API for custom apps, billed in Copilot Credits
summary: Hold: the briefing says the state on arrival is not stated, but Microsoft explicitly requires an administrator to enable consumption billing before Work IQ API usage can begin. The spending-policy paths, Graph operations and consumption licensing are supported; the default-state statements need correction.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing

claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with the supported services such as Cowork, running apps hosted on the Copilot Managed Runtime, and Work IQ API.

claims.where: controls notes; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Spending policies define access and spending limits but do not reserve or allocate credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies control access and spending limits; they don't reserve or allocate credits for a workload, user, or group.

claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator role.
claims.quote: Creating a spending policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role at runtime.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The policy page asks for a monthly user budget limit of at least 2,000 credits per user.
claims.quote: Monthly budget limit for users: Set at least 2,000 credits per user per month

claims.claim: The enablement page documents one-time manual creation of the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: ~5 minutes, one-time per organization. This section creates the Work IQ service principal in your organization, which provisions the Work IQ resource so your applications can request tokens for it.

claims.claim: The MCP overview says the Work IQ service principal is created automatically on first use.
claims.quote: The Work IQ service principal is created automatically in the tenant when you use Work IQ for the first time.

claims.claim: The MCP overview says manual provisioning may be needed before any MCP use, for example for policy configuration.
claims.quote: In some corner cases, such as configuring Work IQ MCP policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center before any MCP use in the tenant, the service principal might not exist yet and policy configuration can fail.

claims.claim: The enablement page lists a usage-based billing plan with an Azure subscription and resource group as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: A usage-based billing plan set up in Copilot Studio with an Azure subscription and resource group assigned.

claims.claim: The Claude integration requires an identity-based spending policy covering its users and the Work IQ API service.
claims.quote: After configuring usage-based billing, create or update an identity-based spending policy covering the approved users and the Work IQ API for custom apps and agents service.

claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is enabled by default for spending policies.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.claim: Service coverage is configured per spending policy, including tenant-wide policies.
claims.quote: Scope a policy to every user in the tenant (`allUsersSpendingPolicy`) or to selected groups (`selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy`). Configure per-service settings that govern or exclude individual AI services within a policy.

claims.claim: Policy and per-user limits can be edited at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > spending policy > Spending limits.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select the Configuration tab. Select the spending policy you want to edit. The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes: Scope; Agents and services; Billing method; Spending limits

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates the spending policy.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}

claims.claim: The policy update supports periodLimit and perUserLimit request-body properties.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: `displayName`, `periodLimit`, `perUserLimit`, and `billingMethods`.

claims.claim: Policy and per-user spending limits can govern selected groups.
claims.quote: Set policy and per-user limits | Limit monthly consumption for selected user groups and the services covered by their policies.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: These spending-policy controls govern who can consume Work IQ API credits and their limits, rather than blocking the REST endpoint itself.
claims.quote: Include Cowork and exclude Work IQ API from a policy when its users shouldn't consume credits through Work IQ API. Review all applicable policies, including the default policy. Excluding a service from one policy doesn't exclude it from other policies.

claims.claim: Excluding Work IQ API from one policy does not exclude it from other applicable policies, including the default policy.
claims.quote: Review all applicable policies, including the default policy. Excluding a service from one policy doesn't exclude it from other policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents tenant-wide blocking of Work IQ MCP.
claims.quote: Block Work IQ MCP tenant-wide only when you intend to stop it for the entire tenant.

claims.claim: Administrators can explicitly enable or disable connector participation in Work IQ paths through tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: Administrators can explicitly enable or disable connector participation in Work IQ paths through tenant-level policies.

claims.claim: REST API use requires a consuming application and authorization for its delegated permission, rather than starting a conversation automatically.
claims.quote:
POST https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/rest/conversations/{conversationId}/chat
Delegated (work or school account) | WorkIQAgent.Ask
Authorization | Bearer {token}. Required.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to check billing method and prepaid capacity, but neither has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Investigate any `QuotaExhausted` error by checking the policy's service selection, limits, billing method and prepaid capacity. The table contains only service coverage and policy/per-user limits.
claims.fix: Replace the After rollout bullet with: 'Investigate any `QuotaExhausted` error by checking the policy's service selection and limits.' Do not add controls-table rows as part of this correction.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center has tenant-level Work IQ MCP policy controls.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.claim: Both policy PATCH operations require CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: | Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All | Not supported. |

claims.claim: Setting state to disabled is the service-removal semantic.
claims.quote: Setting `state` to `disabled` is the removal semantic; the entry is retained in that state, and the collection has no `DELETE`.

claims.claim: The service-setting API refuses to disable a policy's last enabled service.
claims.quote: Disabling the last enabled service is refused with a `409 atLeastOneServiceRequired` response.
